( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 12 February 1981, after the draft finalized by the Fasteners for Consumer Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products and Medical Instruments Division Council. 0.2 T-his standard was first published in 1967 and is being revised to incorporate additional type ( quick release ) and some changes in the figures in the standard as well as to incorporate suggestion received from .time to time. 0.9 In the revision of this standard assistance has been derived following publications issued by Controllerate of Inspection Stores, Ministry of Defence, Government of India: a) Specification b) Specification No. I_N'D/Gs/Navy/lO, and No. IfiD/Gs/373(a). from the General

0.4 This standard contains clauses which call for agreement between the purchaser and the supplier and which permit the purchaser to use his option for selection to suit his requirements. The relevant clauses are 6.2, 6.2,1, 7.1 and 9.1. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. * R llles for rounding off numerical values ( revised). 3

IS : 4274 - 1981 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the materials, shapes and dimensions, workmanship and finish requirements of various types of buckles used for holdalls, shoes, trousers' belts, orthopaedic appliances fitted with belting and saddlery fittings.

4. SHAPES

AND DIMENSIONS

4.1 Various shapes and principal nominal dimensions of the buckles are given in Tables 1 to 10. 5. MANUFACTURE 5.1 The buckles shall be manufactured to shape and size as shown The corners shall be properly chamfered. All the in Tables 1 to 10. The prongs shall be fitted rough and sharp edges shall be removed. in such a way that it permits free movement by hand and shall be pointed for easy entrance in the middle. However, it shall not be unduly pointed as it is likely to cause damage in actual use to the consumer. - *Specification for mild steel wire for general engineering purposes ( third rruision).

5.2 The roller shall be rnade 3 mm shorter than the actual size of the buckle for all buckles of size 25 mm and above and 1.5 mm shorter for all buckles of size less than 25 mm. When fitting the roller to the frame, the frame is not to be reduced. The crew of the prong shall be neatly formed round the bar and the point of the prong shall not extend more than i of its diameter beyond the centre of the roller. The point shall not be too sharp.
6. WORKMANSHIP

AND FINISH
shail be

6.1 Workmanship
free from casting

- The buckles shall be made smooth and flaws, cracks, burrs and other surface defects.

6.2 Finish - When manufactured from cast iron or mild steel, the buckles shall be plated in accordance with Grade 3 of IS : 1068-1968*. The cast iron or mild steel buckles may'also be tinned if required by the purchaser. 6.2.1 At the option of the purchaser, cast brass or brass sheet buckles may be plated in accordance with Grade 3 of IS : 1068-1968* or tinned.

7. SAMPLING 7.1 Sampling
and acceptance criteria for buckles shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. A recommended scheme for the same is given in Appendix A.

8. MARKING 8.1 Each
buckle or packet of buckles .or both, shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the name of manufacturer, initials or trade-mark and the country of manufacture. 8.1.1 The buckles may also be marked with the Standard Mark.

8:.1.2 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

.IS : 4274 : 1981 A-1.2.1 The buckles in the sample shall be selected at random from ;he lot and in order to ensure the randomness of selection, random number As a first st.ep, suitable number of packages ( not tables may be used. less than 10 percent of the total number in the lot subject to a minimum From each of the packages so chosen, of 5 ) shall be chosen at random. an approximately equal number of buckles shall be picked up at random so as to obtain the required number of buckles for the sample. In case random number tables are not available, the procedure given in A-1.2.1.1 may be adopted.
A-1.2.1.1 Starting from any buckle in the lot, count them as 1, 2, 3.... where r is the integral part of Jv/n up to r and so on in one order, ( N being the lot size and n being the number of buckles to be selected ). Every sth buckle thus counted shall be withdrawn to give sample for inspection.

A-2. NUMBER

OF TESTS

AND CRITERIA

FOR CONFORMITY

A-2.1 The buckles selected in accordance with A-1.2.1 shall be examined for workmanship, finish, shape and dimensions. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of this standard if the number of buckles failing in any one or more of the requirements does not exceed the permissible number given in co1 3 of Table Il.
